history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple in the old city of Akola, at the Akola Fort (Shivaji Nagar), revered as the gramdaivat (city deity) — Akola is nicknamed 'Rajeshwar Nagari' after it. Hemadpanti-style stone structure with carved pillars, enshrining an ancient lingam with a visible crack/repair line tied to a local legend about a queen (said to be of 'King Akola Singh') merging into the lingam. BUILDER CONFLICT: one source credits 'Chola Empire King Raj Rajeswar', another says 'constructed during the reign of the Chalukya dynasty' — both unverified; flag. State is MAHARASHTRA (CSV state column held town name).

name: Raj Rajeshwar Temple
town_description: Akola is a city in the Vidarbha region of Maharashtra, nicknamed 'Rajeshwar Nagari' after its gramdaivat. An important trade and administrative centre of western Vidarbha with the historic Akola Fort in the old city, it is served by Akola Junction railway station and a domestic airport.

travel.airport: Akola Airport (~7 km, no scheduled flights at present); nearest international airport Nagpur (~230–250 km)
travel.railway: Akola Junction (~2–3 km) on the Mumbai–Howrah route
travel.road: On NH 6; well connected by road to Nagpur, Amravati and Khamgaon; use auto-rickshaw for the old-city fort area (limited parking)

visitor_information.best_time: October to February; Mahashivratri and Shravan month (especially Mondays) are the main draws
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 5:00 am–12:00 pm, evening 4:00 pm–9:00 pm; aarti 5:30 am and 7:00 pm (single-source; verify)
